sources.entry: Vendure - A headless commerce framework. (Demo, Source Code) MIT Nodejs

summary.one_liner: Vendure is an open-source, headless commerce framework built on Node.js, NestJS and GraphQL for running B2B, D2C, marketplace and omnichannel shops.
summary.what_it_does: The repository is the Vendure source monorepo, containing the @vendure/core framework, a React and TanStack admin dashboard, the CLI, official plugins, and an e2e testing harness. The core covers catalog (products, variants, facets, collections, custom fields), orders (carts, draft orders, fulfillment, returns), multi-location stock, composable promotions, provider-agnostic payment and shipping integrations, and multi-channel, multi-region, multi-currency and multi-language setups. Shop and Admin GraphQL APIs are typed and extensible, and the framework is extended through plugins and service overrides rather than forking. The README says it is not meant to be cloned for building a shop; instead, scaffold a project with npx @vendure/create.
use_cases: Building a B2B or D2C online store
Running a multi-channel, multi-currency storefront backend
Marketplace or omnichannel sales from one API
Adding custom entities and pricing logic to an e-commerce backend
Managing product catalog, inventory and promotions
Serving a custom storefront through a GraphQL API
notable: Plugin contracts and service overrides let you change core behaviour without forking
Introspectable GraphQL schema usable for LLM tool-calling and MCP servers
Multi-channel, multi-region, multi-currency and multi-language from one instance
Extensible React admin dashboard with custom pages and form elements
Plugin license exception allows releasing plugins under any license
caveats: Requires Node.js 22.12+ and a SQL database (PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB or SQLite)
Core is GPLv3; paid Starter, Growth, Scale and Enterprise plans add B2B features such as company accounts, quotes, contract pricing, SSO and audit logs
Vendure Cloud is in design-partner preview with general availability planned for Q1 2027
